Madhu means 'sweet, delicious, nectar, honey'. Vana means 'forest, wood, abode'. Madhab is a compound word, derived from the combination of Madhu (sweet) and Vana (forest). It can mean 'sweet, delicious, nectar, honey', 'God', or 'Lord Vishnu'. It is a common name for both males and females in Hindu culture.
